articles.excerpt: Watch the intro video Ever wanted to watch something on your Mac but hear it in your phone's headphones? It was late, I was watching a show on my MacBook, and my headphones were plugged into my iPhone…
articles.body: Watch the intro video Ever wanted to watch something on your Mac but hear it in your phone's headphones? It was late, I was watching a show on my MacBook, and my headphones were plugged into my iPhone. The Mac speakers would have woken everyone up. So I built PhoneEar 🎧 ▶️ Run it on your Mac 📱 Scan the QR code with your iPhone 👆 Tap "listen" That's it. Your Mac's sound now plays through your iPhone, in whatever headphones are plugged in or paired. ✅ No iPhone app. It runs in Safari ✅ Mac speakers mute automatically ✅ Works over your home Wi-Fi ✅ Free and open source (MIT) ✅ The whole thing is one Swift file The most fun bug along the way: the audio sounded about 9% too fast and kept stuttering.

articles.title: Your Stack Has a Size. Flisk Only Fits One of Them.
articles.excerpt: "We have microservices" is not a sizing input. Twelve services in one Compose file is a different job from twelve services that each own a manifest, a route, and a health check. Flisk is opinionated a…
articles.body: "We have microservices" is not a sizing input. Twelve services in one Compose file is a different job from twelve services that each own a manifest, a route, and a health check. Flisk is opinionated about which of those jobs it wants. This is the decision table I wish every "should we adopt this" thread started with. Three sizes, three tools Your actual stack Better default Why 2–5 services, already containerized Docker Compose One file, no new abstraction, everyone already knows it You already love your Tiltfile Plain Tilt Flisk's job is to write that file. If it exists and works, leave it Local must match the cluster kind, minikube, Skaffold, DevSpace, Garden Those tools target Kubernetes.

articles.body: The Sqlmap tool is an open-source tool that automates SQL injection testing. It can handle what's done manually with a few commands. SQL injection: simply put, if a web application sends the input it takes from the user straight to the database without filtering it, you can write SQL code there. It could be a login form, a search box, a URL parameter, etc. The application runs that code and the data in the database comes out. Installing Docker and SQLmap You need to test against a vulnerable application you set up yourself, not a real system. For this we'll use DVWA (Damn Vulnerable Web Application) . It runs with Docker .

articles.title: From Prompt Injection to Data Leak: Agentic AI Risks
articles.excerpt: When people talked about AI, the focus in most places was on things like model quality, speed, context window. As of today, the topics being discussed have changed a bit. Now these are the questions b…
articles.body: When people talked about AI , the focus in most places was on things like model quality, speed, context window . As of today, the topics being discussed have changed a bit. Now these are the questions being asked more often: What does it have access to? What can it do on its own? What information could it leak? This is exactly where what's called agentic AI comes in. It can read email. It can search for files inside a repo. It can check the calendar. It can make API calls. And this is where the risk begins. In the Global Cybersecurity Outlook 2026 report, 94 percent of respondents say AI will be the factor that changes cybersecurity the most throughout 2026. 87 percent also say that AI-related vulnerabilities are among the fastest-growing risks.

articles.title: Is flisk.sh a Small CLI or a Big Thing?
articles.excerpt: People keep asking the wrong size question about flisk.sh. Is it a platform? A Kubernetes replacement? A new way to build companies? No. It is a CLI. You write a service.json, you run flisk up (the Gi…
articles.body: People keep asking the wrong size question about flisk.sh . Is it a platform? A Kubernetes replacement? A new way to build companies? No. It is a CLI. You write a service.json , you run flisk up (the GitHub README still says tdk up for the same package), and it generates the local Docker and Tilt wiring so those services start on your machine. Production stays on Helm. That is the whole product sentence, and it is a small sentence on purpose. The interesting question is not whether the binary is big. It is whether the mess it refuses to own is big. What is actually small The contract is one manifest per service.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 21, 2008: India launches its 1st mission to the moon with Chandrayaan-1
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 21, 2008, the Indian Space Research Organization launched its first mission to the moon. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 21, 2008, the Indian Space Research Organization launched its first mission to the moon. The mission was named Chandrayaan-1, and it consisted of both an orbiter and an impactor. Chandrayaan-1 launched from the Satish Dhawan Space Center on an Indian rocket called the Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle, or PSLV-XL. (Launch occurred at 8:52 p.m. EDT, though it was about 6:22 a.m. local time at the launch site on Oct. 22.) It arrived in lunar orbit about three weeks later and dropped off the Moon Impact Probe, which crashed into the moon on Nov. 14. The rest of the Chandrayaan-1 spacecraft stayed in orbit, where it collected and transmitted data from the moon to Earth for about a year.

articles.title: Sci-fi legend Alan Dean Foster on his new futuristic adventure 'Lost On Paradise': 'It's paradise until you get there, and then maybe you mess it up' (interview)
articles.excerpt: 'Maybe Paradise isn’t always Paradise.'
articles.body: Few names in the science fiction literary world carry as much weight and respect as author Alan Dean Foster. His award-winning 55-year career as a grandmaster of the genre continues with his latest novel from Blackstone Publishing, " Lost on Paradise ", and we have an exclusive excerpt to share with our readers ahead of its release this week. Foster famously ghost-wrote the first " Star Wars " novelization for George Lucas in 1976 and "Splinter of the Mind’s Eye" in 1978, which was intended to be a low-budget Star Wars sequel should the space opera not become a hit. He’s been a mainstay for go-to fantastic adventures featuring engaging characters, dynamic plotlines, and imaginative worlds for six decades.
